In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

.

Commentary on Surah An-Naba' (The Tidings)

It is Meccan.

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿About what are they asking one another? About the great news﴾. Its meaning: "About what are they asking one another?" The nun was assimilated into the mim, and the alif was dropped, so it became ʿamma (عَم).

Al-Zajjaj said: Its wording is that of a question, but its meaning is the magnification of the matter, like the speaker who says: "What is Zayd like?" (أَي شَيْء زيد؟), meaning how great Zayd is.

In the tafsir it is related that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sent and called the polytheists to monotheism (tawhid), some of them began asking one another: "With what was Muhammad sent? And to what does he call?" So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse.

The meaning of "they ask one another" (yatasa'aluna) is that some of them ask others.

As for His words: ﴿about the great news﴾, it has been said that its meaning is: about the great news. The scholars differed concerning "the great news." Abu Salih related from Ibn ʿAbbas that it is the Qur'an. From Qatadah it is related that it is the Resurrection (al-ba'th), and this is the view of Abu al-ʿAliyah, al-Rabi' ibn Anas and a group. From al-Hasan it is related that he said: it is prophethood (al-nubuwwah). The first two views are well known.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

From al-Hasan it is related that he said: it is prophethood (al-nubuwwah). The first two views are well known.
And His saying, ﴿about which they differ﴾, means: among them are those who affirm it and among them are those who deny it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 78, verses 4–5:

And His saying: ﴿No! They will come to know. Then, no! They will come to know.﴾ Al-Hasan said: It is a threat following a threat.

And it is related from al-Dahhak that he said: His saying ﴿No! They will come to know﴾ means: the disbelievers.

And His saying ﴿Then, no! They will come to know﴾ means: the believers. But the apparent meaning is that both are for the disbelievers.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 78, verses 4–5:

And His saying: ﴿No! They will come to know. Then, no! They will come to know.﴾ Al-Hasan said: It is a threat following a threat.

And it is related from al-Dahhak that he said: His saying ﴿No! They will come to know﴾ means: the disbelievers.

And His saying ﴿Then, no! They will come to know﴾ means: the believers. But the apparent meaning is that both are for the disbelievers.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 78, verse 6:

Allah the Exalted's words: ﴿Have We not made the earth a resting place?﴾ When Allah the Exalted informed of their disagreement concerning the Qur'an and the Resurrection, and their disagreement about the Resurrection was in acceptance and denial, and their disagreement concerning the Qur'an, that it is sorcery or poetry or soothsaying, Allah the Exalted mentioned the proofs against them regarding monotheism, and that what He sent down is truth and sincerity, and He enumerated His blessings upon them, so that they would acknowledge it and be thankful to Him.

Allah the Exalted's words: ﴿resting place﴾ meaning: a spread-out expanse and a bed, and the blessing lies in its being made submissive and smooth for them.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 78, verse 7:

And His saying: ﴿And the mountains as pegs﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: When God Most High created the earth, it began to tilt (tukfaʾu), and Ibn ʿAbbas moved his hand [to illustrate]. So God created the mountains and fixed them into it (arsāhā bihā), that is, He made them firm (athbatahā). Thus they are the pegs of the earth, just as a thing is fixed to a wall by a peg (watad).

And His saying: ﴿And We created you in pairs﴾. That is, kinds (aṣnāf). The place of the blessing is that some of them find tranquility (sukūn) with others. The man and the woman are a pair (zawj), and likewise the heaven and the earth, the night and the day, and other creations. It was also said that "azwājan" means compatible (mutaʾallifīn): you find your spouses agreeable, and your spouses find you agreeable.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 78, verse 9:

And His saying: ﴿And We made your sleep a rest (subat)﴾. Tha'lab said: "Cessation from your works (qat'an li-a'malikum). The original meaning of sabat is stretching out and stillness."

The meaning is that they cease from movement at night, so they become still and rest. It was also said: sabatan means rest (raha).

The poet said:

"And a folded-up saddle-girth of a mount: as for its day, it is sabt (a day of rest), and as for its night, it is zamil (a traveling companion)."

I.e., qati' (a cutting off, a cessation).

And His Exalted saying: ﴿And We made the night as a garment﴾ — that is, a covering for you. It is mentioned in the manner of metaphor (majaz). Its rationale is that the darkness of the night envelops every person just as a garment envelops him, so He called it a garment by way of metaphor.

And His saying: ﴿And We made the day a time for livelihood﴾ means: a seeking of livelihood and a pursuit of livelihood. The meaning is that it is the time in which they live and go about their affairs.

And His saying: ﴿And We built above you seven strong (heavens)﴾ — meaning: the seven heavens.

And His saying: ﴿strong﴾ — meaning: firm and solid. And it is related in the reports that the thickness of each heaven is a five-hundred-year journey.
Wa-qawluhu: ﴿wa-ja'alnā sirājan wahhājā﴾ means: We made the sun a blazing, dazzling lamp.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 78, verse 14:

And His saying: ﴿And We have sent down water from the pressing clouds﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "They are the winds." The reason for calling them by this name is that the winds fertilize the clouds so that rain comes forth from them, so it is as if the rain came from the winds. The second opinion is that the pressing clouds are the clouds. This is also narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, and it is the view of Mujahid and a group.

Al-Mubarrad said: "They are named 'pressing' (mu'sirat) because they are squeezed (yan'asir) by the rain little by little." It was also said: "min al-mu'sirat" means "bi-l-mu'sirat," i.e., water pouring forth from the pressing clouds, ﴿in torrents﴾.

And His saying: ﴿in torrents﴾ means pouring forth, some of it following upon the rest.

And it is narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "The best of Hajj is the 'ajj and the thajj." The 'ajj is raising the voice with the talbiyah, and the thajj is the shedding of blood (sacrificial animals).

And it is narrated from Qatadah that "the pressing clouds" is the sky. This is a strange (gharib) opinion.

His words: ﴿So that We may bring forth thereby grain and plants, and gardens of thick entwined foliage﴾. That is, "entwined" (multafifa). The singular of al-alfaf is laff, and the "entwined" ones are those whose parts enter into one another.

His words: ﴿So that We may bring forth thereby grain and plants, and gardens of thick entwined foliage﴾. That is, "entwined" (multafifa). The singular of al-alfaf is laff, and the "entwined" ones are those whose parts enter into one another.
Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, the Day of Decision is an appointed time﴾. That is, an appointed term for all creatures, and it is the Day of Resurrection.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 78, verse 18:

And His saying: ﴿The Day the Trumpet is blown﴾. Al-Naqqash (al-Naqqash) mentioned in his exegesis that Israfil (ʿalayhi al-salam) descends and sits upon the rock of Bayt al-Maqdis, and the spirits are placed in the Trumpet like swarms of bees, and the circumference of the mouth of the Trumpet is as wide as the distance between the heavens and the earth, five hundred years' journey. Then he blows, and the spirits come out of it and return to their bodies.

And His saying: ﴿then you will come forth in multitudes﴾. Mujahid said: "Group after group."

And His saying: ﴿And the sky is opened﴾, meaning: it was made into paths. It is also said: the gates of the sky were opened for the descent of the angels.

And His saying: ﴿so it becomes gateways﴾, meaning: they were paths, as we have explained.

And His saying: ﴿And the mountains will be set in motion, and they will become a mirage﴾ — that is, scattered dust. It is also said: it will become like a mirage, which you think is something while it is nothing.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 78, verse 21:

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, Hell has always been a place of ambush﴾. The scholars of the language (ahl al-lughah) said: "Anything that is in front of you is a rasad (an ambush, a lying-in-wait place)." The meaning is that it is the place where the disbelievers are kept under watch for the descent of punishment upon them.

It is related from some of them: "O owner of the rasad, remember the rasad." It was also said: "Marsadan" means that they are lying in wait with punishment, in the sense that it is prepared for them.
And His saying: ﴿For the transgressors, a place of return﴾ — meaning: a place of turning back. It is said: "āba ilā makān kadhā" means he returned and turned back.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 78, verse 23:

And His saying: ﴿Remaining therein for ages (ahqab)﴾. Al-huqbah (an age, a long period) in the language is a portion of time, like al-hin (a while).

Mutammim ibn Nuwayrah said, lamenting his brother Malik:

(And we were like the drinking companions of Jadhimah for an age of time, until it was said they would never part.)

That is, a portion. As for what is transmitted in the exegeses from the early generations (al-salaf) regarding the meaning of huqb: the most apparent of the opinions is that it is eighty years, each year being three hundred and sixty days, each day being a thousand years. This is related from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAs, Saʿid ibn Jubayr, Qatadah and others, and similarly from Abu Hurayrah.

And from some of them: that it is three hundred years, each year being three hundred and sixty days, each day being like the duration of this world. And from some of them: some eighty-odd years.

If it is said: does this verse indicate that the punishment of the disbelievers ends when the ahqab have passed? The answer comes in several aspects. (First): its meaning is "remaining therein for ages, not tasting therein coolness or drink," that is, they will be punished with this type of punishment for ages, and there are other ages for the rest of the types of punishment; this was said by al-Mubarrad.

The second aspect: that the meaning of "remaining therein for ages" is that the Fire will not abate from them; so when the Fire abates and they are increased in blaze, they will remain forever.

The third aspect: what Ibn Kaysan said, which is that its meaning is "remaining therein for ages, following ages that do not end, ever."

Al-Nahhas said: this is the clearest of the opinions.

On His words, ﴿They will not taste therein any coolness (bardan)﴾: Tha'lab said, "sleep." The Arabs say, "The sleep (al-bard) prevented him," meaning sleep. And the poet said:

(If you wish, I will forbid women to all of you, and if you wish, I will not give you cold water (naqakh) or sleep (bardan).)

Naqakh is sweet, pure water. It is also said that "bardan" means rest (rahah). And it is said that "bardan" means that the fierce heat of the blaze and its flame will not be cooled for them.

On His words, ﴿nor any drink (sharaban)﴾: that is, thirst will not be quenched for them.

.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 78, verse 25:

And His saying: ﴿Except boiling water and dark, foul liquid﴾. Abu 'Ubayda said: al-hamim (boiling water, the scalding liquid) is hot water, and from it comes al-humma (fever), and from it is the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And a shade of black smoke﴾. It has also been said: al-hamim is that their tears are gathered together and they are given it to drink.

And His saying: ﴿wa-ghassaqan﴾, meaning: thick pus. It has also been said: it is the pus of the people of the Fire. And it has been said: al-hamim is that which is at the extreme of heat, and al-ghassaq is that which is at the extreme of cold, which is az-zamharir (bitter, freezing cold), so they are tormented with each of the two punishments.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 78, verse 26:

And His saying: ﴿a recompense corresponding (to their deeds)﴾, meaning: a recompense that matches their deeds.

Ibn Zayd said: They did evil, so they were recompensed with evil.
The Almighty's saying: ﴿Indeed they used not to expect a reckoning﴾, i.e., they did not fear it. We have already explained that "hope" (rajaʾ) carries the meaning of "fear" in an earlier passage.
And His saying: ﴿And they denied Our signs with a [persistent] denial﴾, i.e., "denial" (takdhiban). Al-Farra' said: it is an eloquent Yemeni dialect.

And His saying: ﴿And everything We have enumerated in a Book﴾ is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And everything We have enumerated in a clear Imam﴾, meaning: We have set it out in the Preserved Tablet (al-lawh al-mahfuz).

And His saying: ﴿So taste, for We will not increase you except in punishment﴾. That is: it is said to them, "Taste the punishment," for it will not be cut off from you, and you will be increased only in punishment.

The poet said:

(I believed her and I called her a liar... and a man may benefit from his lying.)
Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, for the righteous is an attainment of success.﴾ That is, فوزا (fawzan, success), and al-mafaz (المفاز) is the place of success (fawz).
Its saying: ﴿Gardens enclosed with walls, and grapevines﴾ has a clear meaning, and we have already explained it.

And His saying: ﴿And full-breasted maidens of equal age﴾. Al-kawā'i' (the full-breasted ones) are al-nawāhid (those whose breasts are firm and rounded); it is said: "jāriyah kā'ib," meaning a girl whose breast has protruded like a knucklebone (ka'b), and she is nāhid.

And His saying: ﴿atrāban﴾ means of one age (lidāt), and it is said: daughters of thirty-three years.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 78, verse 34:

And His saying: ﴿And a cup overflowing﴾ means full, related from Mujahid. ʿIkrimah said: pure. And it is related from some of them: successive. The first opinion is more apparent, and it is related from Ibn ʿAbbas. And from him also that he said: "I often heard al-ʿAbbas say: 'Give me to drink, O slave-girl, the cup, and fill it (wa-dhqi, from al-dahq).'" And also from him: that he called for a cup, and the slave-girl brought it full, and he said: "This is the dahq."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 78, verse 35:

And His saying: ﴿They will not hear therein any vain talk or lying﴾. Al-laghw (vain talk) is: speech that is cast aside (al-kalam al-mutarrah).

And His saying: ﴿kidhdhaban﴾ means: they will not call one another liars. It has also been read as "kiddhaban" with the lighter pronunciation, and its meaning is simply falsehood (al-kadhib) and nothing else. The poet says:

(So I believed her and I disbelieved her... and a man is benefited by his lying.)

That is, by his lying (kadhibihi).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 78, verse 36:

And His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿A recompense from your Lord, a gift sufficient (ʿaṭāʾ ḥisāban)﴾. That is: a gift that is sufficient. It is said: "So-and-so gave me until I said, 'Enough for me' (ḥasbī)," meaning: until I said, "Enough." Qatadah said: "A gift sufficient (ʿaṭāʾ ḥisāban)" means: abundant. The poet said, regarding the first meaning:

(We feed the young man of the tribe if he is hungry... and we satisfy him if he is not hungry.)

And His saying: ﴿A recompense from your Lord, a gift﴾ means: give recompense (jazāʾ), and give a gift (ʿaṭāʾ).

.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 78, verse 37:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, the Most Merciful﴾. Both are read in the nominative (marfu'). It is also read: "Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, the Most Merciful," with the first in the genitive (majrur) and the last in the nominative.

Both are also read in the genitive: "Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, the Most Merciful." The reasoning (wajh) of the first reading is that His saying, ﴿Lord of the heavens and the earth﴾, is nominative as the subject (mubtada'), and "the Most Merciful" is its predicate (khabar). The reasoning of the second reading is that His saying, ﴿Lord of the heavens and the earth﴾, is genitive, following His saying, ﴿from your Lord﴾, and His saying, ﴿the Most Merciful﴾, is a new subject (mubtada'). The reasoning of the third reading is that both are genitive, following His saying, ﴿from your Lord﴾.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They will not possess from Him any address﴾, meaning: they will not speak with Allah, and they will be prevented from speaking with Him. It was also said: ﴿they will not possess from Him any address﴾ means they will not intercede for anyone except with His permission, as He said later on.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 78, verse 38:

The words of the Most High: ﴿The Day when the Spirit (al-Ruh) and the angels stand in rows﴾. Mujahid said: "The Spirit is a creation who resemble the children of Adam, but they are not the children of Adam." It was also said: "It is Jibril (peace be upon him)." It was also said: "It is a creation among the creation of God, not created before the Throne, greater than it. On the Day of Resurrection it will stand in a row, and all the angels in a row." It was also said: "ṣaffan" means "in rows." The place of a servant's prayer is called ṣaff, because it is the place of the rows.

His words: ﴿They will not speak﴾, meaning: they will not intercede, that is, the angels. It was also said: they will not speak at all.

His words: ﴿except one whom the Most Merciful has permitted﴾, meaning: permitted to intercede and to speak.

His words: ﴿and he speaks what is right﴾, meaning: what is true. It was also said: it is "There is no god but God." The meaning is that they will not speak except with permission, or they will speak what is right, which is "There is no god but God."

The saying of the Exalted: ﴿That Day is the Truth﴾ — meaning: the Resurrection is the true Day, and the meaning of "truth" here is that it is certainly going to happen, without doubt.

And His saying: ﴿So whoever wills may take a return to his Lord﴾ — meaning: a good place of return, through obedience and worship.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 78, verse 40:

And the words of Allah the Exalted, ﴿Indeed, We have warned you of a near punishment﴾: that is, the Fire, and everything that is coming is near.

And His words ﴿The Day when a man will look at what his hands have sent forth﴾: that is, what his hands have sent forth of good and evil.

And His words ﴿And the disbelievers will say, "Oh, I wish I were dust!"﴾: Ja'far ibn Burqan narrated from Ibn al-Ahmar, from Ibn 'Abbas, that Allah the Exalted will gather creation on the Day of Resurrection, including the animals, birds, humans and jinn. When the two weighty ones (al-thaqalan, i.e. humans and jinn) have been settled in their places, He will say to the birds, the beasts and the animals: "Become dust!" So they will become dust. Then the disbeliever will say: "Oh, I wish I were dust!"

He (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Abu Muhammad 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad informed us, Abu Sahl 'Abd al-Samad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Bazzaz informed us, Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Zakariyya al-Ghadafari informed us, al-Dabari, that is Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, informed us, 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, from Ma'mar, from Ja'far ibn Burqan... the hadith.

It is also said: the disbeliever here is Abu Jahl.

Al-Naqqash mentioned in his Tafsir, from al-Hasan ibn Waqid, who said: the disbeliever will say: "Oh, I wish I were a pig, so that I would become dust," and the dust will say to him: "No, and no honour for you," meaning: you will not be like me.

The same has been related from al-Suddi as well.

It is also reported from some scholars that the meaning of His words ﴿Oh, I wish I were dust!﴾ is: "Oh, I wish I had not been resurrected."

Regarding the ḥuqub (an extended period of time) which we mentioned, two reports have come from Ibn 'Umar, who said: Let each of you act in obedience and let him not speak as if he will enter the Fire and then leave it, for no one enters the Fire and then leaves it except after remaining for ahqab (periods of time). He mentioned the ḥuqub as we explained, from the mention of eighty.

The second report is what has been related from Ibn Mas'ud concerning the enduring of bliss for the people of Paradise and punishment for the people of the Fire. It is what al-Suddi narrated from Murrah, from 'Abd Allah, who said: If the people of the Fire knew that they would remain in the Fire for as many years as there are pebbles, and then would come out of it, they would rejoice; and if the people of Paradise knew that they would remain for as many years as there are pebbles, and then would come out of it, they would grieve.

Both reports are gharib (rare/weak in transmission).
